disclaimer: These rules describe patterns in wearable data compared with a person's own usual range. They are educational, are not diagnoses, and do not estimate the likelihood of any condition.

rules.name: Resting heart rate drift
rules.summary: Your resting heart rate has been running above your own usual range for several days in a row.

physical: Recovery after exercise can feel slower
Energy may dip through the afternoon
mental: Stress may feel closer to the surface

remedies: Aim for a consistent sleep and wake time this week
Reduce late-day caffeine and alcohol and see if the trend eases
Add short, easy walks and keep hard workouts lighter for a few days
Try a 5-minute slow-breathing break once or twice a day
Stay hydrated through the day

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of heart conditions
hereditaryModifiers.note: Because heart conditions run in your family, this pattern is surfaced a little sooner. This is about sensitivity only and is not a diagnosis.

rules.name: HRV decline
rules.summary: Your heart rate variability has stayed below your own usual range, which can reflect extra strain or reduced recovery.
symptoms: Trouble switching off in the evening

mental: Mood may feel flatter or more irritable

remedies: Protect a wind-down routine before bed
Space out intense training with lighter or rest days
Limit alcohol, especially in the evening
Build in short breaks and breathing exercises during busy days
Get some daylight and gentle movement every day
rules.specialist: General physician; a sleep or sports medicine clinician if it continues
sources: Cleveland Clinic (health library on heart rate variability)
Mayo Clinic (patient education on stress and recovery)

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of heart conditions
hereditaryModifiers.note: Family history can make it worthwhile to notice this pattern earlier. It does not mean anything is wrong.

rules.name: Sleep fragmentation
rules.summary: Your sleep has been more broken up than your own usual pattern, with more restless periods overnight.
symptoms: Waking several times during the night
Morning headaches or a foggy feeling

physical: Appetite and energy can feel off

remedies: Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet
Avoid screens and heavy meals in the hour or two before bed
Cut back on caffeine after midday
Keep alcohol away from bedtime
Write down worries earlier in the evening so they stay off your mind at night
rules.specialist: General physician or sleep medicine specialist
sources: American Academy of Sleep Medicine (patient resources)

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of sleep problems
hereditaryModifiers.note: Sleep patterns can run in families, so this is surfaced slightly earlier. It is not a diagnosis.

rules.name: Low deep sleep
rules.summary: The deep sleep your wearable estimates has been below your own usual range for a while.

physical: Energy may be lower through the day
mental: Memory and focus can feel less sharp
Mood may be more easily affected

remedies: Keep a steady bedtime and wake time, including weekends
Finish intense exercise a few hours before bed
Avoid alcohol close to bedtime
Keep your room cool and dark
Get morning daylight to support your body clock
rules.specialist: General physician or sleep medicine specialist
sources: American Academy of Sleep Medicine (patient resources)

rules.name: SpO₂ dips
rules.summary: Your overnight blood-oxygen readings have been lower than your own usual range on several days.
symptoms: Waking up with a dry mouth or sore throat
Feeling short of breath with light activity

physical: Energy may be lower during the day

remedies: Check that your wearable fits snugly and the sensor is clean, since fit affects readings
Try sleeping on your side instead of your back
Avoid alcohol and sedating substances before bed
Keep your sleeping space well ventilated
rules.specialist: General physician or pulmonologist; a sleep specialist if breathing at night is a concern
sources: Mayo Clinic (patient education on breathing and sleep)

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of breathing or lung conditions
hereditaryModifiers.note: Family history can make it sensible to notice this sooner. Wearable oxygen readings are estimates and can vary with fit.

rules.name: Low activity
rules.summary: Your daily movement has been lower than your own usual range for an extended stretch.

physical: Muscles and joints may feel stiffer
mental: Stress may feel harder to shake off

remedies: Add a 10-minute walk after a meal
Take short movement breaks every hour if you sit for work
Pick one active habit you enjoy and do it at a fixed time
Use stairs or walk part of your commute when you can
Invite a friend along to make it easier to stick with
sources: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (physical activity basics)

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of diabetes or metabolic conditions
hereditaryModifiers.note: Regular movement is especially helpful when metabolic conditions run in the family. This only adjusts how soon the pattern is shown.

rules.name: Elevated respiratory rate
rules.summary: Your breathing rate during sleep has been higher than your own usual range for several days.
symptoms: A stuffy nose or mild cough

physical: Breathing can feel less easy during exertion

remedies: Rest more and ease off intense exercise for a few days
Drink fluids and keep your room comfortably humid
Practise slow, relaxed breathing before bed
Avoid smoke and strong irritants
Note any cold-like symptoms, since they often explain short-term changes

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of breathing or lung conditions
hereditaryModifiers.note: Family history can make it sensible to notice this pattern earlier. It is not a diagnosis.

rules.name: Irregular sleep schedule
rules.summary: Your bedtime has been shifting more than usual from night to night.
symptoms: Trouble falling asleep at your usual time
Energy that is uneven across the day

physical: Body clock may feel out of step
Appetite and energy can be less steady
mental: Focus may vary from day to day

remedies: Pick a target bedtime and move toward it in small steps
Keep your wake time steady, even on weekends
Get bright light soon after waking
Dim lights and screens in the evening
Plan late nights ahead and protect the following morning
rules.specialist: General physician or sleep medicine specialist
sources: American Academy of Sleep Medicine (patient resources)
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (sleep and sleep disorders)

hereditaryModifiers.label: Family history of sleep problems
hereditaryModifiers.note: Sleep timing can run in families, so this is shown a little sooner. It does not indicate a condition.
